context.title: Sent Out From Antioch
context.summary: The Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul. On Cyprus a sorcerer is struck blind and the governor believes. In Pisidian Antioch Paul preaches in the synagogue; when many Jews reject the message, he turns to the Gentiles.
context.background: From here on Saul is called by his Roman name, Paul (v. 9), and soon becomes the lead figure. Luke's Greek title for the governor of Cyprus (KJV 'deputy') is proconsul, correct for a province run by the Roman Senate. John Mark leaves the team at Perga (v. 13).

customs.note: Readings from the Law and the Prophets were followed by an invitation for a qualified visitor to give a word of exhortation.
A public gesture of disowning a place that had rejected the message, as Jesus instructed (Luke 9:5).

watchFor: 'A light of the Gentiles' (v. 47) quotes Isaiah 49:6.
'Filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost' despite persecution (v. 52).

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Barnabas
people.summary: Son of consolation, the surname of Joses, a Levite (Acts 4:36). His name stands first on the list of prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (13:1).

people.name: Herod Antipas
people.summary: Herod’s son by Malthace (Matt. 14:1; Luke 3:1, 19; 9:7; Acts 13:1).

people.name: Lucius
people.summary: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch (Acts 13:1), and Paul’s kinsman (Rom. 16:21).

people.name: Manaen
people.summary: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch.

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: Surnamed Niger, i.e., “black,” perhaps from his dark complexion, a teacher of some distinction in the church of Antioch (Acts 13:1-3). It has been supposed that this was the Simon of Cyrene who bore Christ’s cross.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: John
people.summary: The evangelist; “John whose surname was Mark” (Acts 12:12, 25). Mark (Marcus, Col. 4:10, etc.) was his Roman name, which gradually came to supersede his Jewish name John.

people.name: Elymas
people.summary: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus.

people.name: Sergius
people.summary: A “prudent man” (R.V., “man of understanding”), the deputy (R.V., “proconsul”) of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-13).

people.name: Samuel
people.summary: Heard of God. The peculiar circumstances connected with his birth are recorded in 1 Sam. 1:20. Hannah, one of the two wives of Elkanah, who came up to Shiloh to worship before the Lord, earnestly prayed to God that she might become the mother of a son.

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Kish
people.summary: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul (1 Sam. 9:1, 3; 10:11, 21; 14:51; 2 Sam. 21:14). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Pontius
people.summary: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

places.name: Antioch (Syria)
places.summary: In Syria, on the river Orontes, about 16 miles from the Mediterranean, and some 300 miles north of Jerusalem. It was the metropolis of Syria, and afterwards became the capital of the Roman province in Asia.

places.name: Cyrene
places.summary: A city (now Tripoli) in Upper Libya, North Africa, founded by a colony of Greeks (B.C. 630). It contained latterly a large number of Jews, who were introduced into the city by Ptolemy, the son of Lagus, because he thought they would contribute to the security of the place.

places.name: Cyprus
places.summary: One of the largest islands of the Mediterranean, about 148 miles long and 40 broad. It is distant about 60 miles from the Syrian coast. It was the “Chittim” of the Old Testament (Num. 24:24).

places.name: Seleucia
places.summary: The sea-port of Antioch, near the mouth of the Orontes. Paul and his companions sailed from this port on their first missionary journey (Acts 13:4).

places.name: Salamis
places.summary: A city on the south-east coast of Cyprus (Acts 13:5), where Saul and Barnabas, on their first missionary journey, preached the word in one of the Jewish synagogues, of which there seem to have been several in that place.

places.name: Paphos
places.summary: The capital of the island of Cyprus, and therefore the residence of the Roman governor. It was visited by Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary tour (Acts 13:6).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Pamphylia
places.summary: Paul and his company, loosing from Paphos, sailed north-west and came to Perga, the capital of Pamphylia (Acts 13:13, 14), a province about the middle of the southern sea-board of Asia Minor.

places.name: Perga
places.summary: The capital of Pamphylia, on the coast of Asia Minor. Paul and his companions landed at this place from Cyprus on their first missionary journey (Acts 13:13, 14), and here Mark forsook the party and returned to Jerusalem.

places.name: Antioch (Pisidia)
places.summary: In the extreme north of Pisidia; was visited by Paul and Barnabas on the first missionary journey (Acts 13:14). Here they found a synagogue and many proselytes.

places.name: Pisidia
places.summary: A district in Asia Minor, to the north of Pamphylia. The Taurus range of mountains extends through it.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Iconium
places.summary: The capital of ancient Lycaonia. It was first visited by Paul and Barnabas from Antioch-in-Pisidia during the apostle’s first missionary journey (Acts 13:50, 51).

events.title: First Missionary Journey
events.summary: Passage: Acts 12:24–14:28. People: Paul, Barnabas, John. Place: Antioch (Syria), Perga, Attalia, Pamphylia. Lasted about 1 year.

events.title: First missionary journey begins
events.summary: Passage: Acts 12:24–13:3. People: Holy Spirit, Manaen, Lucius, Simeon, John, Paul and others. Place: Antioch (Syria).

events.title: Barnabas and Saul go to Cyprus
events.summary: Passage: Acts 13:4–12. People: Elymas, Paul, Barnabas, Sergius, John. Place: Paphos, Salamis, Cyprus, Seleucia.

events.title: Mission to Antioch in Pisidia
events.summary: Passage: Acts 13:13–52. People: Barnabas, John, Paul. Place: Iconium, Antioch (Pisidia), Paphos, Jerusalem. Lasted about 3 months.
